edges.effect_quant: A 2020 systematic review of next-generation sequencing studies included 12 observational cohorts with 708 PPI users and 11 interventional cohorts with 180 PPI users and found consistent taxonomic shifts toward oral-type organisms, with fecal alterations summarized across 19 cohorts comprising 790 PPI users; in a 2024 prospective intervention study of 16 healthy adults, esomeprazole caused a 42-fold increase in gut Streptococcus anginosus abundance and significantly increased oral-to-gut microbial translocation.
edges.population: adult chronic or short-term proton pump inhibitor users studied with sequencing-based gut microbiome profiling, including healthy volunteers and observational cohorts
edges.mechanism: Acid suppression weakens gastric microbial filtering and allows more oral and upper-gastrointestinal organisms to survive and seed distal gut compartments, shifting community composition toward dysbiosis-prone taxa such as streptococci and enterococci.
edges.summary: Among common medications, proton pump inhibitors have one of the clearer reproducible associations with gut microbiome disruption. The effect is usually described less as a loss of diversity than as a compositional drift toward oral-origin bacteria and away from several butyrate-associated or health-associated taxa.
edges.caveats: Not every study shows major diversity loss, and many human cohorts are observational or short-term. The microbiome shift does not mean every PPI user develops clinical harm, but it does support the idea that long-term acid suppression is a real dysbiosis-promoting exposure.

evidence.citation: MackeL et al 2020 Aliment Pharmacol Ther
evidence.notes: Systematic review: the effects of proton pump inhibitors on the microbiome of the digestive tract-evidence from next-generation sequencing studies.

new_entities.name: Gut microbiome dysbiosis
new_entities.description: An unfavorable shift in gut microbial community composition associated with impaired resilience or increased disease susceptibility.
